correctness.rationale: Starting from exact unordered hard-core hopping, the sign-even configurations form an invariant subspace with block matrix [[0,2R],[2R^T,2(R^TR-2I)]]. The unsigned complete-graph incidence matrix has RR^T=(m-2)I+J and squared singular values 2m-2 (one) and m-2 (m-1). Each 2x2 block has Rabi leakage F_q(t)=4q/(q^2+4)sin^2(t sqrt(q^2+4)), yielding the displayed exact weighted formula. The sine bound and t=pi/(2sqrt((m-2)^2+4)) sandwich the scaled all-time leakage at 4. Classical lumpability has exact outgoing rates 4(m-1) and 2 and solves C(t)=1/(2m-1)+(2m-2)/(2m-1)exp(-(4m-2)t). The standalone verify.py directly constructs full independent Hamiltonian and classical generator and passes 36 paired comparisons with maximum errors 9.44e-15 and 3.11e-15, respectively. Limit verified by explicit algebra; finite tests only corroborate.

value.rationale: The exact and sharp all-time quantum leakage O(1/m) from the nonedge-paired sector is an unusual confinement effect in a high-degree hopping network with no attractive potential, while rate-one classical exclusion almost surely unpairs on the inverse-degree time scale. The inverse-size observation window and asymptotic coefficient 4 are motivated by the natural combinatorial number of available single hops, not an arbitrary parameter slice. This provides a benchmark for coherent two-particle dynamics and illustrates a precise configuration-space interference mechanism. It is not merely another finite numerical spectrum or a restatement of generic strongly-regular graph methods.
